extracted.intended_audience: Authors, referees, and readers of Nature Communications (research community submitting to or reviewing for the journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Journal-level policy describing the default publication of peer review files alongside research articles and the options and rationale for reviewer anonymity, signing, and author double-blind review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default publication of peer review files
rubrics_metrics.description: For manuscripts received from November 2022 onwards, the peer review files will be published alongside every published Nature Communications research article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting in 2016 authors could opt in; from Nov 2022 onward publication of the exchanges between authors and reviewers will be the default for accepted research articles. The editorial frames this as making peer review files part of the official scientific record and preserving reviewer comments as valuable scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee anonymity and signing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees will still have the option to remain completely anonymous, to sign their reports, and/or to choose to be acknowledged by name as part of our reviewer recognition scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer choices about anonymity/signing/acknowledgement remain optional even when peer review files are published. The policy preserves flexibility for referees who wish to remain anonymous while enabling recognition for those who opt in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author option for double-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Communications will continue to offer authors the possibility to opt-in double blind peer-review, during which their identities remain anonymous to the referees during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who prefer double-blind review may opt in; this option remains available alongside the policy to publish peer review files for accepted papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review comments as preserved scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review comments represent valuable scholarship that should be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial endorses the view that reviewer reports are scholarly contributions worth preserving and making part of the official record; it cites prior commentary arguing for publication of peer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish reports to expose caveats and interpretive disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Making reports and the response from the authors public shows that valid potential caveats or limitations of the study have been raised and discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors and referees cannot reach complete agreement on interpretation, publishing the exchange reveals discussed caveats and limitations and informs readers about differing viewpoints on data interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable readers to assess robustness of conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Armed with the peer review file, each reader can better critically assess the robustness of the conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published reviewer reports and author responses give readers additional material to judge whether reported findings are adequately interpreted and supported, increasing transparency around the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit authors by documenting their rebuttals and arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Making the back and forth between authors and referees available also benefits authors, as it allows them to bring forward arguments in support of their view that might otherwise be difficult to logically integrate within a paper’s narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing the exchange provides authors a way to surface arguments and clarifications that are not suitable for the main manuscript, thereby augmenting the value of the published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide recognition to reviewers who wish it
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing peer review files provides greater recognition to reviewers should they wish to be acknowledged for their contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alongside anonymity and signing options, the policy highlights that published reports can offer credit/recognition to reviewers via the journal's reviewer recognition scheme when reviewers opt to be named.
